item.title: Untargeted Metabolomic Analysis of Acute Kidney Injury After Maze-Inclusive Cardiac Surgery
item.description: CONCLUSION: Tryptophan metabolism is significantly upregulated in patients with AKI after maze-inclusive cardiac surgery. Kynurenic acid presumed in this study represents as candidate metabolite of postoperative AKI, providing an opportunity to gain insight into the underlying pathophysiology through further targeted metabolomics.

item.description: Compressed sensing MRI seeks to accelerate MRI acquisition processes by sampling fewer k-space measurements and then reconstructing the missing data algorithmically. The success of these approaches often relies on strong priors or learned statistical models. While recent diffusion model-based priors have shown great potential, previous methods typically ignore clinically available metadata (e.g. patient demographics, imaging parameters, slice-specific information). item.description: Carbonyl reductase 1 (CBR1) is an NADPH-dependent enzyme that reduces doxorubicin to doxorubicinol and is therefore of pharmacological interest as a modulator of anthracycline metabolism. Panaxfuraynes A and B are tetrahydrofuran-type polyacetylene sophorosides from Panax ginseng C.A. Meyer whose biological activities have remained uncharacterised since their isolation in 2009. Here we identify both compounds as inhibitors of human CBR1 and examine the structural basis of their activity. The...

item.description: The metallic 1T phase of MoS2 provides basal-plane activity and high conductivity that are absent in the semiconducting 2H polymorph, making it attractive for applications in electrocatalysis and energy conversion. However, its intrinsic metastability readily drives relaxation to the 2H ground state, and previous attempts to stabilize 1T-MoS2 have yielded only transient domains or localized perturbations without durable phase retention. item.title: After ENRICH: Evidence boundaries and unresolved questions for early minimally invasive evacuation in lobar intracerebral hemorrhage
item.description: The ENRICH trial renewed interest in early minimally invasive surgery (MIS) for spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), with its clearest treatment signal observed in selected patients with lobar hemorrhage. However, prior and subsequent surgical trials differ substantially in patient population, hematoma location, timing, technique, device, endpoint selection, and procedural execution. item.description: Silkworm pupae are continuously generated as a major byproduct of the silk industry and have traditionally been utilized as a food resource in Korea. item.description: Microwave-driven carbothermal shock (CTS) synthesis has attracted considerable attention as an ultrafast route for nanomaterial production. However, controlling nanoparticle nucleation and growth during the extremely short microwave irradiation period remains challenging. item.title: Effects of virtual reality-based exercise on biomechanical and functional outcomes: a narrative review of randomized controlled trials
item.description: This study was conducted as a structured narrative review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating virtual reality (VR)-based exercise and rehabilitation. PubMed and the Research Information Sharing Service were searched for peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025. Predefined search terms and eligibility criteria based on the population, intervention, comparison, and outcome framework were applied to identify relevant studies for narrative synthesis. item.title: Electroacupuncture for Procedural Anesthesia: A Scoping Review of Stimulation Parameters and Anesthetic-Sparing Outcomes
item.description: CONCLUSION: This review maps potentially promising stimulation parameters but cannot establish the efficacy or clinical superiority of EA. The 2/100 Hz protocol with structured pre-operative induction should be regarded as a hypothesis-generating starting point for standardized trials, for which this evidence map provides a design framework. Kilohertz-frequency stimulation, studied only experimentally, is a hypothesis for future research.

item.title: Alcohol consumption and mortality after mitigating sick-quitter bias: A 19-year nationwide cohort study of Korean adults
item.description: BACKGROUND AND AIM: The lower mortality risk often observed among low-level drinkers remains controversial because estimates may be distorted by sick-quitter bias and poor baseline health among abstainers. We examined whether a dose-response association between alcohol consumption and mortality persisted among drinking groups after applying several strategies to reduce these biases in a nationwide cohort of Korean adults.

item.title: SPIRIT-A: An Extension of SPIRIT 2025 for Acupuncture Clinical Trial Protocols
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: SPIRIT-A provides structured reporting recommendations addressing key methodological considerations in acupuncture clinical trial protocols. Its development followed internationally recognized methodological standards and is expected to enhance the completeness and reproducibility of acupuncture RCT protocols and facilitate their broader dissemination and use.

item.description: Plants, as sessile organisms, must continually adapt to fluctuating temperatures to ensure survival. The plasma membrane-localized receptor-like kinase FERONIA (FER) coordinates diverse physiological processes and responses to various biotic and abiotic stresses. However, the role of FER in plant adaptation to elevated temperatures remains largely unexplored. Here, we report that FER is indispensable for plant growth and survival at warm temperatures. item.description: CONCLUSION: Impaired quality of life, and radiographic evidence of bone erosion were identified as independent risk factors for gout flare in this prospective cohort study. These findings highlight the importance of comprehensive clinical assessment to identify high-risk patients for future flares and optimize individualized management strategies.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Our WSI-level AI model offers a robust, efficient solution for diagnosing metastatic GC and CRC in ascitic cytology. It addresses limitations of manual and patch-based methods, supports clinical decision-making, and enhances diagnostic accuracy.

item.title: Efficacy and Safety of Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy for Fatigue and Neurocognitive Symptoms in Long COVID: A Prospective Observational Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: The significant reduction in fatigue, improvements in several cognitive function domains, mental health outcomes, and post-COVID-19 symptoms suggest that HBOT could be a potential therapeutic option for long COVID.

item.description: CONCLUSION: MASLD was associated with an increased risk of bladder cancer, and this association remained significant among never smokers after excluding cases within 3 years.

item.title: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes of Community-Onset and Hospital-Onset Sepsis Patients: The Korean Nationwide Sepsis Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study presents the first nationwide data on the epidemiology of community-onset and hospital-onset sepsis in Korea. Compliance with time-based sepsis bundles was associated with lower mortality. These findings underscore the need for standardized sepsis care and government policies to enhance early recognition and timely management of sepsis in Korea.

item.title: DTC1225, a novel benzothiazole-based compound, ameliorates MASLD by restoring metabolic-redox homeostasis and promoting hepatic lipid remodeling
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: DTC1225 ameliorates MASLD-associated hepatic pathology through multifaceted mechanisms involving coordinated modulation of autophagy-related pathways, lipid metabolism, and redox homeostasis, accompanied by favorable hepatic lipid remodeling. These findings provide a critical rationale for further development of DTC1225 as an innovative therapeutic candidate for MASLD and its associated complications.

Here, a potential pathogenic ATP10B R303W variant was identified from 45-year-old Korean man and investigated in a familial case of early-onset PD. item.description: CONCLUSION: Compared with high-intensity rosuvastatin monotherapy, moderate-intensity rosuvastatin and ezetimibe was non-inferior regarding regression of coronary atherosclerotic plaque (Supported by Hanmi Pharmaceutical co., ltd; ROSUZET-IVUS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03169985).

item.title: Public and private reputation systems for limiting centralized corruption
item.description: Corruption is widely recognized as a major challenge in human institutions. To prevent its spread, measures such as increasing transparency have attracted growing attention. Here, we develop an evolutionary game-theoretic framework with a reputation mechanism to address centralized corruption and sustain cooperation. item.title: RSP1141, a reversible non-covalent BTK inhibitor, suppresses GPVI-mediated platelet activation
item.description: AIMS: The glycoprotein VI (GPVI)-Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) axis drives collagen-induced platelet activation and arterial thrombosis. Approved BTK inhibitors act irreversibly on Cys481, raising concerns over off-target kinase inhibition, C481S resistance, and bleeding. We aimed to identify a non-covalent, reversible BTK inhibitor with antiplatelet activity and to define quantitatively its selectivity within the platelet GPVI cascade.

item.title: Longitudinal Changes in Physical Performance with Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Coronary Artery Disease
item.description: CONCLUSION: Baseline TUG impairment and within-group longitudinal TUG deterioration were associated with adverse MASLD, CAD, and fat distribution profiles. While causal relationships cannot be established, TUG performance may serve as a functional marker reflecting metabolic and cardiovascular health status in older adults.

Recently, black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) have attracted increasing attention as biological agents for manure reduction and resource recovery. item.description: Riparian floodplains store substantial quantities of soil organic carbon (SOC), yet their response to future changes in hydrologic regimes remains uncertain. item.description: Freeway diverge areas require complex decisions under tight spatiotemporal constraints, often resulting in late-initiated maneuvers among novice drivers. To evaluate how pavement guidance markings influence diverging behavior, this study proposes a two-layer lane-change evaluation framework combining longitudinal spatial feasibility, represented by the Dynamic Minimum Diverging Length (DMDL) model, with lateral trajectory consistency, represented by a fitted trajectory envelope. item.description: Peer victimization is embedded in classroom peer networks, yet not all students with lower classroom peer acceptance are equally vulnerable. This study examined whether student-level vulnerabilities moderated the association between classroom peer acceptance and peer-nominated victimization among South Korean elementary school students. item.description: The rapid growth of modern broiler chickens, driven by intensive genetic selection, has led to a high incidence of metabolic myopathies, resulting in significant economic losses in the poultry industry. These myopathies are fundamentally driven by localized bioenergetic failure, mitochondrial dysfunction, and oxidative stress within muscle fibers. Therefore, establishing a reliable in vitro model to dissect these cellular mechanisms and evaluate targeted protective compounds is crucial. This...

item.title: Maternal functional connectivity relates to child behavioral problems and parenting stress across child developmental stages
item.description: Previous studies have indicated maternal brain changes during pregnancy and the postpartum period, but associations between maternal brain function and ongoing caregiving remain underexplored. This study examined how maternal functional connectivity (FC) patterns are associated with child behavioral problems and parenting stress across child developmental stages. item.title: Real-world effectiveness of emicizumab prophylaxis in Korean patients with severe hemophilia A
item.description: CONCLUSION: Emicizumab prophylaxis achieved effective bleeding prevention and high target joint resolution rates in Korean patients with severe hemophilia A, validating real-world effectiveness when administered according to evidence-based criteria.

item.title: Comparative incidence and severity of iodinated and gadolinium-based contrast reactions using actual administration counts: A five-year single-center study
item.description: CONCLUSION: ICM showed a higher incidence of reported reactions than GBCAs, but severe reaction rates per administration were similar. Prior ICM reaction history may inform GBCA risk assessment; integrated cross-modality screening requires further validation.

item.description: Motion sickness is commonly assessed through repeated subjective ratings, such as the Misery Scale (MISC), which yield symptom time-series. These trajectories are typically reduced to scalar indicators, but what each indicator captures, and how the indicators relate to one another, remains poorly understood, making it difficult to match indicators to research questions. item.description: Streamline tractography from diffusion magnetic resonance imaging is the standard technique for mapping the structural connections of the human brain, but raw tractograms contain systematic streamline-density biases that undermine quantitative connectivity analysis. item.title: The Independent and Interactive Effects of Networks of Family and Friends on Mental Distress in Older Korean Americans
item.description: Social networks are vital supports for older adults, yet the interactive roles of family and friend networks remain understudied. Drawing on social compensation theory, this study examined the independent and interactive associations with mental distress among older Korean Americans (N = 1,924). Multivariate regression showed that family (B = -.12, p < .001) and friend networks (B = -.12, p < .001) were independently associated with mental distress. item.title: Transmission dynamics of Nipah virus in Bangladesh and India, 2001-2026: Systematic review and inference on reproduction number, offspring dispersion, and serial interval
item.description: CONCLUSION: NiV transmission is self-limiting on average and highly overdispersed, suggesting that a disproportionate share of onward transmission arises from a small number of cases. This epidemiological profile supports targeted containment measures, including contact tracing and quarantine, for effective NiV outbreak control.

item.title: Quantum-enhanced wafer failure prediction in semiconductor fabrication
item.description: In recent years, rapid advancements in semiconductor manufacturing have underscored the critical need for robust quality control to maintain high yields and reliability in wafer production. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Extrarenal involvement is present in nearly half of patients at LN diagnosis, however, it does not appear to influence renal response, DORIS remission, or the long-term risk of renal or extrarenal flares.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In POAG eyes, the mCT reduction was localized to the papillomacular and inferotemporal peripapillary regions, which are critical areas for central visual function and topographically distinct from structural retinal ganglion cell loss. This pattern was not observed in eyes with long AXLs, presumably because significant axial-elongation-induced thinning restricts further discernible changes. Future studies are needed to determine the clinical significance of mCT alterations in POAG.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Robot-assisted RIRS was feasible and safe for treating a residual superior calyceal stone after multiple prior endourological interventions. item.title: HER2-Positive Biliary Tract Cancer in 2026: From Genomic Profiling and HER2 Phenotyping to Treatment Selection and Sequencing
item.description: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is actionable in biliary tract cancer (BTC), but protein overexpression, ERBB2 amplification, and activating mutations are not therapeutically equivalent. This review integrates genomic profiling, HER2 phenotyping, and contemporary HER2-directed evidence into a practical framework for treatment selection and sequencing in 2026.

item.title: Multidisciplinary control of Doege-Potter syndrome associated with unresectable liver metastases from a pelvic solitary fibrous tumor
item.description: Doege-Potter syndrome (DPS) is a rare paraneoplastic form of non-islet cell tumor hypoglycemia associated with solitary fibrous tumors (SFTs), usually mediated by tumor-derived high-molecular-weight insulin-like growth factor II. item.title: Chromosome 14q loss is associated with adverse survival and a distinct transcriptional phenotype in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma
item.description: CONCLUSION: RNA-seq-inferable 14q loss identifies a clinically adverse subgroup of Japanese IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, is complementary to MGMT promoter methylation, and is associated with a proliferation-high, oxidative-phosphorylation-low transcriptional state. The absence of this association in TCGA underscores the need for validation in additional population-diverse cohorts before clinical implementation.
